item.title: Lost Sepik fish rediscovered after 40 years
item.description: A freshwater fish found only in Papua New Guinea’s Sepik River has been rediscovered after disappearing from scientific records for more than 40 years. The Spinach Pipefish, known scientifically as Microphis spinachioides , was last scientifically recorded in 1985.
item.content:encoded:
A freshwater fish found only in Papua New Guinea’s Sepik River has been rediscovered after disappearing from scientific records for more than 40 years.

The Spinach Pipefish, known scientifically as Microphis spinachioides , was last scientifically recorded in 1985.

It was rediscovered during a two-week survey in the Lower Sepik River led by Papua New Guinea researcher Jerrica Agebigo, an MPhil research student with the PNG University of Technology and the New Guinea Binatang Research Centre.

The search involved scientists working closely with local communities, including fishers, village elders, women who catch freshwater prawns and market vendors.

The breakthrough came at Imbando Village along the Main Sepik River, where local woman Helen Asu helped researchers locate the fish.

Helen regularly catches freshwater prawns using a traditional hand net known locally as Umben .

After researchers showed her photographs of pipefish, she recognised the species and agreed to look for it during her next fishing trip.

The following morning, she caught two pipefish while collecting freshwater prawns along a heavily vegetated riverbank and alerted the research team.

Three Spinach Pipefish were observed over two consecutive mornings in the same area.

Two specimens were retained for further scientific examination, while photographs were also taken.

Australian ichthyologist Dr Gerry Allen later confirmed the fish’s identity after examining the photographs and identifying key features of the species.

The rediscovery has raised hope that a population of the rare fish may still survive in parts of the Sepik River system.

Agebigo says the knowledge and support of local communities was critical to the success of the search.

“Without her knowledge, initiative, and willingness to assist, the rediscovery may not have been possible,” she said of Helen Asu.

Researchers say the discovery also highlights the importance of traditional ecological knowledge in scientific research.

However, communities along the Sepik River have raised concerns about declining native fish populations and increasing numbers of introduced species.

They identified sedimentation, logging, mining, habitat damage and the loss of riverbank vegetation as major threats.

Researchers say further surveys are needed across the Sepik-Ramu Basin to determine the fish’s distribution and estimate the size of its remaining population

They also plan to develop a method using environmental DNA from water samples to detect the species without having to catch the fish.

item.title: Angau Hospital receives 36 new ventilators worth K1.8 million
item.description: Patients struggling to breathe at Angau Memorial Provincial Hospital will have improved access to critical care following the arrival of 36 new ventilators valued at about K1.8 million. The portable machines will be used in the emergency department, intensive care unit, nursery and acute medical and surgical wards.
item.content:encoded:
Patients struggling to breathe at Angau Memorial Provincial Hospital will have improved access to critical care following the arrival of 36 new ventilators valued at about K1.8 million.

The portable machines will be used in the emergency department, intensive care unit, nursery and acute medical and surgical wards.

They are intended for patients who cannot breathe sufficiently on their own and need urgent support to stay alive while they recover.

Australian Consul-General to Momase, Brenton Kanowski, said the ventilators were life-saving equipment for health workers.

“These ventilators are life-saving tools for our health professionals here at the hospital,” he said. For Dr Steven James, director of medical services at the Morobe Provincial Health Authority, the equipment will strengthen the hospital’s ability to respond to critically ill patients.

“For us, receiving this very vital equipment will enable our acute care teams to better support patients in our care services,” James said.

The ventilators are portable, allowing health workers to move them between patients and departments when needed.

Health authorities are also considering using some of the machines in district hospitals, which could allow seriously ill patients outside Lae to receive urgent breathing support closer to home.

But James said the equipment would only be effective if staff were trained to use it and the machines were properly maintained.

“The person using the machine must understand how to operate it properly,” he said.

The ventilators were sourced through Save Our Supplies, an Australian charity based in Brisbane, and transported to Papua New Guinea on an Australian Navy ship.

The donation is part of a long-running health partnership between Australia and Morobe.

Australia has also supported the redevelopment of Angau Hospital, including planned work on wards and the construction of a standalone pharmacy.

For patients and their families, however, the immediate value of the new equipment is simple: better access to breathing support when it is needed most.

item.title: PPC Rubiang leads Kundiawa police in town beautification

item.content:encoded:
Kundiawa town got a full scrub-down on Saturday, 29 th August as Provincial Police Commander Superintendent, Mazuc Maipe Rubiang swapped the patrol car for a rubbish bag and hit the streets with his officers.

The Kundiawa police officers rolled out a large-scale cleanup across the town, collecting waste and clearing rubbish hotspots. Police trucks were on standby to haul the rubbish to proper disposal sites.

PPC Rubiang said this wasn’t just about picking up trash, the exercise was about changing mindset.

Officers spent time talking with market vendors, shop owners and residents, pushing a simple message: keep your space clean, and Kundiawa stays safe.

“Law and order aren’t only about arrests.

“A clean town is a healthy town. And keeping Kundiawa clean is everyone’s job, not just police or council.” Supt Rubiang said

He said the cleanup is part of a wider push by police to work closer with the community and local authorities.

"We hope today’s effort sets the tone for ongoing cooperation with residents and businesses taking ownership to maintain what was cleaned", he said.

Supt Rubiang said the tidier, healthier Kundiawa will attracts businesses and gives residents pride in their town.

item.title: Parliament faces historic decision on Bougainville’s future
item.description: The political future of the Autonomous Region of Bougainville is now before Papua New Guinea’s Parliament. This follows the tabling of the 2019 Bougainville Referendum result and the presentation of the Bougainville Bipartisan Committee report in Parliament yesterday.
item.content:encoded:
The political future of the Autonomous Region of Bougainville is now before Papua New Guinea’s Parliament.

This follows the tabling of the 2019 Bougainville Referendum result and the presentation of the Bougainville Bipartisan Committee report in Parliament yesterday.

Committee Chairman Dr Allan Marat presented the report, outlining the work carried out following the referendum.

“For all members of Parliament, of the 11th Parliament, this will be the most consequential question that we will have to decide upon, the vote that we take.” Opposition leader James Nomane said.

“It’s incumbent on the executive government and also on all leaders to understand the issues that have been placed before us, the gravity of the situation, the desires of the people of Bougainville through a 97.7 referendum result, that we all have to take the time from now until the next Parliament sitting,” he added.

Nomane urged Parliament not to simply glaze over the document or merely flick through its pages, but to give it careful and thoughtful consideration.

The decision will have long-term consequences for the country and must be made responsibly and in unity.

item.title: Nomane calls for no further delay on Bougainville vote
item.description: Opposition Leader James Nomane is calling on the Government to provide a clear timeline for Parliament to vote on the 2019 Bougainville Referendum result. Nomane made the call in Parliament on Thursday following the historic tabling of the referendum result, the Joint Consultation report and the Melanesian Framework agreement.
item.content:encoded:
Opposition Leader James Nomane is calling on the Government to provide a clear timeline for Parliament to vote on the 2019 Bougainville Referendum result.

Nomane made the call in Parliament on Thursday following the historic tabling of the referendum result, the Joint Consultation report and the Melanesian Framework agreement.

He says Parliament must clearly outline when the debate and vote will take place, with all MPs present to make the decision.

“We also ask that the executive government, also not kick the can down the road and deal with this vote” Nomane said

“They must confirm all members of parliament be present at the next sitting to vote. This issue has created a lot of anxiety, a lot of ambiguity, a lot of confusion,” Nomane added.

Nomane says the vote will determine Bougainville’s political future and will have major consequences for Papua New Guinea.

The PNG and Bougainville governments are expected to meet in October to agree on a date for the parliamentary vote.

Nomane says there should be no further delays on the issue, which he describes as one of the most important decisions facing the country.

item.title: PNG and Vanuatu agree to share experiences in the space of public prosecution
item.description: Informal discussions over a cup of coffee have been spiced with a Memorandum of Understanding, bridging together the Papua New Guinea and Vanuatu Public Prosecutors' Offices. The Memorandum of Understanding [MOU] was signed between PNG Public Prosecutor Helen Roalakona and Vanuatu Public Prosecutor Simcha Boe on Tuesday in Vanuatu’s capital - Port Vila.
item.content:encoded:
Informal discussions over a cup of coffee have been spiced with a Memorandum of Understanding, bridging together the Papua New Guinea and Vanuatu Public Prosecutors' Offices.

The Memorandum of Understanding [MOU] was signed between PNG Public Prosecutor Helen Roalakona and Vanuatu Public Prosecutor Simcha Boe on Tuesday in Vanuatu’s capital - Port Vila.

The first female public prosecutor of Papua New Guinea speaking to this newsroom in Port Vila gave an insight into the agreement, “MOU signed between the Office of Public Prosecutor of Vanuatu was about capacity building and professional exchange between both offices.

“The Public Prosecutor of Vanuatu approached me after a PILON [Pacific Islands Law Officers Network] meeting in October last year, asking if we could give support to his office to deal with matters which would require outside prosecution.

“What was a discussion over a cup of tea ended up with a memorandum of understanding where the focus is on capacity building, professional development, and exchange of ideas and skill sets.

“What it does now is enable our prosecutors from PNG to travel to Vanuatu and assist them with some of their cases, and also their lawyers and corporate service staff [will travel to PNG to] learn about how we run our operations,” PNG’s public prosecutor said.

All expenses of the trip from Port Moresby were paid by the Australian Government under its Law and Justice Sector Program.

When the question was put to Ms Roalakona about the benefits of Office of PNG Public Prosecutor entering into such an agreement, she said, “for OPP PNG, it will expose our prosecutors to be able to prosecute in other jurisdictions, especially within the Pacific and give them the opportunity to have horizontal relationships with our colleagues and counterparts in the other Pacific countries, especially within the Melanesian [Spearhead] Group.

"For the colleagues in Vanuatu is basically to help them with skills and capacity building in the area of complex cases because we have a variety of criminal offending that happens in Papua New Guinea, of which they don’t have this kind of scale in Vanuatu, but it gives them upskilling and confidence to prosecute highly complex cases when they are confronted with them.”

The MOU with Vanuatu is the second for Papua New Guinea inked similar with another Melanesian Country. The first was with Solomon Islands, signed in October last year in Port Moresby.

item.title: PM apologizes to Bougainvilleans at historic referendum results tabling
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape apologized to the people of Bougainville for the pain and suffering associated with the 10 year crisis, eventually leading to the region’s push for independence. He made this apology in his opening statement in Parliament at the historic tabling of the 2019 Bougainville Referendum results on Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister James Marape apologized to the people of Bougainville for the pain and suffering associated with the 10 year crisis, eventually leading to the region’s push for independence.

He made this apology in his opening statement in Parliament at the historic tabling of the 2019 Bougainville Referendum results on Thursday.

Mr Marape also called for the members to carefully examine the Joint consultation report and the melanesian framework agreement, and not be rushed into making a decision at voting time.

The historic tabling of the Bougainville Referendum results, including the Joint Consultation Report and the Melanesian Framework Agreement - signal the official process for the PNG Parliament to consider the region’s push for Independence.

Prime Minister James Marape also paid tribute to former Prime Ministers and National and Bougainville leaders who contributed to peace.

He told the house that whatever the decision parliament makes, ultimately, Peace must always prevail.

PM Marape urged Members of Parliament not to approach the eventual vote with predetermined positions, but to study the documents, consult their people and consider both Bougainville’s aspirations and the wider country.

He says members must not be rushed, adding Parliament now has the opportunity to carefully examine the Referendum result, the Joint Consultation Report, the Melanesian Framework, and to debate their contents and implications before making its decision at a future sitting.” Prime Minister Marape said the Government envisages

Upon consultation between both governments, Parliament is expected to return in October to allow members and governors to contribute fully before an eventual Vote.

A date for a vote on the 2019 Bougainville Referendum results is expected to be set in October, following a meeting between the Papua New Guinea and the Autonomous Bougainville Governments.

Prime Minister James Marape announced in Parliament, at the tabling of the results, and that of the Joint Consultation report and the Melanesian Framework Agreement.

item.title: Mendi Munhiu prioritizes maternal health care
item.description: Six new maternity wings have been established across health centers in the Mendi-Munhiu district in Southern Highlands province. The improved facilities will provide health workers with a more suitable environment to conduct antenatal checks, monitor pregnancies, assist with deliveries and respond to complications.
item.content:encoded:
Six new maternity wings have been established across health centers in the Mendi-Munhiu district in Southern Highlands province.

The improved facilities will provide health workers with a more suitable environment to conduct antenatal checks, monitor pregnancies, assist with deliveries and respond to complications.

Mendi Munhiu, MP Raphael Tonpi said the first of the new maternity facilities at Topa Health Centre in Karinz local level government, has already been completed and commissioned.

“Every mother deserves safe and quality health care, regardless of whether she lives in town or in a remote village,” he said.

Each of the six health centres will also be supported with a brand-new ambulance to strengthen emergency referrals and ensure mothers and other patients can be transported quickly to higher-level health facilities when necessary.

Mr Tonpi said the maternity facilities are developed through a partnership between the District’s Development Authority and the Provincial’s Health Authority.

He said K300,000 has been allocated to each maternity facility to support construction and improve the standard of maternal healthcare available in the district.

Mr Tonpi confirmed that the remaining four maternity wings are expected to be commissioned in the coming weeks at Munhiu, Wais, Pingirip and Mogol health centres.
